recon.notes: Homeless promoter: nothing is published on a Goldiloxx-owned site; the two configured doors are ticketing-platform searches scoped to the name. The Instagram handle (@goldiloxx__) appears only in the RedEye description text and was NOT scraped from Instagram. Run 20260909-072307 for this parser: urlCount 2, totalEvents 4 raw, duplicatesRemoved 3, rawBearEvents 1, bearEvents 1 — the 4 raw records are the Chicago event read from /e/goldiloxx-chicago, /e/goldiloxx-chicago-2 and their two /tickets pages, folded to one 'GOLDILOXX Chicago' 2026-09-20T02:00:00.000Z (= Sep 19 21:00 CDT) at Jackhammer, city chicago, ticketUrl https://www.sickening.events/e/goldiloxx-chicago/tickets, image = the -2 listing's cloudinary URL. Sickening JSON-LD 'organizer' is the venue (Jackhammer / The Hole Chicago), never Goldiloxx — a promoter-attribution trap for any code that trusts organizer.name. Sickening soft-404s (HTTP 200 shell on any slug), so a deleted /e/ page and 'no events' look alike unless the search's empty-state text or a control search is checked.

coverage.basis: Door 1 (RedEye JSON API, configured): meta.pagination.total_count 1 / total_pages 1 → exactly 1 upcoming event, GOLDILOXX SINGLET NITE, Sep 26 2026, Red Eye NY. Door 2 (Sickening ?q=goldiloxx, configured): 2 cards / 2 event slugs (goldiloxx-chicago, goldiloxx-chicago-2) that are one event, GOLDILOXX Chicago, Sep 19 2026, Jackhammer — the config comment counted 2 links on 2026-08-04 and the 2026-09-07 page cache holds the same 2 slugs, so the count has been stable at 2 listings / 1 event. Soft-404 discrimination in the same session: nonsense ?q=zzzzqqqq → 58,104 B, 0 slugs, 'No events found with these filters'; control ?q=vampires → 60,369 B, 1 slug; goldiloxx → 62,947 B, 2 slugs. Second-door cross-check: the RedEye event page and both Sickening /e/ pages (JSON-LD + visible date strings) and the three flyers agree with the feed/search rows on date, time, and venue; the only deltas are the duplicate -2 listing (explained: venue basement cross-post, tickets redirect to the primary) and the RedEye row being absent from the 2026-09-07 cache (explained: published 2026-09-09T15:24Z). Total published = 2 distinct events. No past listings on either door: RedEye returns only the upcoming row, Sickening's search block is headed 'Upcoming Events'.

traps.label: second 'GOLDILOXX Chicago' card / /e/goldiloxx-chicago-2 (organizer 'The Hole Chicago (Basement of Jackhammer)')
traps.why: The same Sep 19 2026 event at Jackhammer published twice by the venue group: once under Jackhammer and once under its basement bar The Hole. Identical name, startDate, endDate, location, description and flyer; the -2 page has no offers and its /tickets link 302s to /e/goldiloxx-chicago/tickets. It must fold into the primary, never become a second event.

expect.note: It IS crawled (2 of the 4 raw records in the run come from this slug and its /tickets redirect) and correctly deduplicated into goldiloxx-chicago-2026-09-19; keyed by title|startDate|bar it is indistinguishable from the primary, so a run containing the primary satisfies this trap. A run with TWO Goldiloxx Chicago events on 2026-09-19 is the failure.

traps.label: EARLY BEAR / TIER 1 / TIER 2 / DOOR offers and the /e/goldiloxx-chicago/tickets page
traps.why: Four price tiers in the JSON-LD offers[] and a dedicated /tickets page (93,624 bytes, same MusicEvent JSON-LD plus a tier table) that the search card links to as 'Tickets'. They are prices for the one Sep 19 event, not events; the /tickets page is a second crawl of the same event (2 of the 4 raw records in the run).

traps.label: HTTP 200 'Event Not Found' shell on any /e/ slug (13,815 bytes)
traps.why: Sickening returns 200 for a fabricated slug (/e/definitely-not-a-real-event-xyz123) with a JS-app shell whose only text is the not-found message, and the search page also returns 200 for a nonsense query (58,104 bytes, 0 /e/ links, 'No events found with these filters'). A deleted Goldiloxx listing or a broken search both look like a healthy 200; only the empty-state text, the link count, and a same-session control search (?q=vampires → 1 link) tell 'no events' from 'site broken'.

The parser is configured on the ?q=goldiloxx door and discoveryAllowedPatterns ['goldiloxx'] blocks every other slug; anything on the unfiltered page that is not goldiloxx is another promoter's event, not a Goldiloxx miss.
